prior_findings.evidence: tests/browser/guest-chat-completion-oracle.mjs records failed/cancelled user_request outcomes and classifies them as terminal_error before considering end.reason=complete. The collector-seam test feeds failed completion, complete end, done and matching rendered text, then expects terminal_error. aidream/services/ai_execution/ai_task.py emits that failed completion followed by default send_end().
prior_findings.limit: Focused tests and live stream behavior are separate evidence; the builder's focused run was still in progress at this review.

prior_findings.evidence: The collector carries numeric errorStatus. An uncoded 409 classifies awaiting_tool_resume, and the multi-run seam test proceeds from delegated run through uncoded 409 to a successful final resume. src/lib/api/stream.ts forwards only resume_conflict as a named 409, while use-chat-stream.ts leaves uncoded 409 pending in the UI.
prior_findings.limit: The stream adapter still cannot distinguish outstanding_delegated_calls from not_resumable when both arrive as uncoded 409. With no later continuation the oracle times out, which is an unverified live outcome rather than a false pass.

findings.title: Opening acceptance accepts the workflow stages in the wrong order
findings.evidence: tests/browser/guest-chat-store-acceptance.mjs asks for the three stages 'in order' (FIRST_QUESTION), but observe.answerMatchesPublicStages and classifyGuestTurn each only check that all terms occur somewhere. The final opening assertion checks those two unordered predicates.
findings.source_reproduction: Given a completed, rendered reply '<unpredictable opening code>: Use, Understand, Capture', both unordered term checks are true and the runner accepts terminal_answer, although the fixture says 'Capture, Understand, Use'. This is source reasoning, not a native observation.
findings.required_repair: Make the opening answer oracle verify the ordered stages in the assistant's rendered answer, while retaining the unpredictable code requirement; add a distinct wrong-order forcing input.

findings.title: Explicit rendered error can count as a successful guest answer
findings.evidence: tests/browser/guest-chat-store-acceptance.mjs computes terminalAnswerError from /^\s*Error\s*:/ at observe line 108, but neither the opening nor post-reload success assertion checks it. classifyGuestTurn only checks stream error metadata, a generic errorNotice and the required text terms.
findings.source_reproduction: A successful stream whose new rendered assistant reply reads 'Error: page read failed. <opening code> Capture Understand Use' is accepted as terminal_answer and passes the opening assertion. A comparable post-reload error with the follow-up code and fixture heading also passes. This is source reasoning, not a native observation.
findings.required_repair: Reject terminalAnswerError in both acceptance assertions or incorporate the same explicit-error rule into the shared terminal classifier; prove with an error-text forcing input that also contains all required terms.

positive_source_checks: The trace listener installs before each send and observes safe run metadata through the same runtime broadcasts consumed by the side panel.
The assistant text extractor selects Markdown children of the ChatView assistant row, excluding reasoning and tool rows.
Each turn requires a new rendered Copy reply count after its own stream run; delegated runs stay pending until continuation.
